title: A globally generated projective bundle is H-projective
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal E$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent] generated by finitely many global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], and let $\pi:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)	o S$ be its projective-bundle morphism [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], using the relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj] of the quasi-coherent symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Then $\pi$ is H-projective, i.e. projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections'

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family $s_0,\ldots,s_r\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal E)$ ($r\geq0$; for $\mathcal E=0$ take $r=0$, $s_0=0$). By [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], its evaluation map $\varepsilon:\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E$ is surjective as a map of sheaves. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] gives the induced algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}(\varepsilon):\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)})\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)$ with $\operatorname{Sym}(\varepsilon)\circ j=j\circ\varepsilon$; on an affine open $U$ with $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$, clause (b) identifies it with the $R$-algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_R(R^{\oplus(r+1)})\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal E(U))$ sending $\iota(e_i)$ to $\iota(s_i|_U)$. Since $\operatorname{Sym}^n_R$ is spanned by products of $n$ degree-one elements and is the degree-$n$ summand [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], this map is degree-preserving and is the identity of $R$ in degree $0$. Surjectivity as a map of sheaves in each degree $n$: a section of $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathcal E)$ over an affine $U$ is a finite sum of products $\iota(t_1)\cdots\iota(t_n)$ with $t_k\in\mathcal E(U)$; by the definition of generation each $t_k$ is, on the members of an open cover, an $\mathcal O$-linear combination of the $s_i$, and on a common refinement by affine opens (finitely many $t_k$) each product, hence the sum, is the image of a polynomial expression in the $\iota(e_i)$. Thus $\operatorname{Sym}(\varepsilon)$ is a degree-preserving graded algebra map, surjective as a map of sheaves.

proof.text: By the surjective-graded-map clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] (whose proof treats a graded map surjective as a map of sheaves), the map of Step 1 induces a closed immersion $\iota:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}))$ over $S$, i.e. compatible with the structural maps of [def-nagata-relative-proj]. By [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] the target, with its structural map, is the relative projective space $\mathbf P^r_S\to S$ of the relative-Proj interface. Thus $\pi=p\circ\iota$ with $p:\mathbf P^r_S\to S$ the relative-Proj structural map.

source.place: Lemma Tag 087S, proof paragraph beginning 'If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections'

proof.text: The relative-Proj $\mathbf P^r_S$ is identified over $S$ with $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], the projective space used in [def-kun-projective]. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O^{\oplus(r+1)})$ on $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. By clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] (index the basis $e_0,\ldots,e_r$), $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z,\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z})\cong\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$, $\iota(e_i)\mapsto T_i$; it preserves degree since both degree-$n$ pieces are spanned by products of $n$ degree-one elements [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ itself, $\operatorname{Proj}_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}(\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z})\cong\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ (an isomorphism of graded rings induces one of the Mathlib Proj schemes [def-nagata-affine-proj]). Let $g:S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ be the unique map. The algebra $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)})$ is identified with the coefficientwise pullback $g^*\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z}$ in the sense of [def-nagata-graded-algebra-pullback-data]: for an affine $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ take $\alpha:\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_r]\to\mathcal B(U')\cong R[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ (clause (b) and the polynomial leaf over $R$), $T_i\mapsto T_i$; in degree $n$, $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[T]_n\to R[T]_n$ is an isomorphism of free $R$-modules on the degree-$n$ monomials, and these maps commute with restriction because restriction is coefficientwise and fixes each $j(e_i)$. Hence [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] gives an isomorphism $\mathbf P^r_S=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\cong S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}(\mathcal A_{\mathbf Z})\cong\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)$ under which $p$ becomes the first projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Composing $\iota$ of Step 2 with this isomorphism gives a closed immersion $i:\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};S)$ (a closed immersion followed by an isomorphism, directly from [def-weil-closed-immersion]) with $\pi=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ i$. This is exactly the data of [def-kun-projective] with $N=r$, so $\pi$ is H-projective.

split_report.summary: Split the globally generated case of Stacks Tag 087S into three proof steps. Finite global generators give a sheaf epimorphism from a finite free module; the induced symmetric-algebra map is degree-preserving and surjective as a map of sheaves (local argument in Step 1). Relative-Proj functoriality gives a closed immersion into the relative-Proj projective space of the free module, and the relative-Proj base change along $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ identifies that with the base-change projective space used by the H-projective definition. No new nodes; item statement unchanged. (Maintainer reader Q60: Step 3 added for the identification $\mathbf P(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)})=\mathbf P^r_S$ against [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], which the delivery omitted.)
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the Tag 087S paragraph beginning “If $\mathcal{E}$ is generated by finitely many global sections”: the surjection $\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal E$ (Step 1), the induced closed immersion $\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\to\mathbf P(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n})$ (Step 2), and the identification $\mathbf P(\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n})=\mathbf P^{n-1}_S$ (Step 3).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q60-bad9e6448 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 087S, the paragraph beginning 'If E is generated by finitely many global sections', the item, every cited node statement, the proof of clause (3) of prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality, the parent and the unit sk-i-curve-zero. The statement is the exact globally generated sub-case and is not weakened. Edge cases E=0 (P(E) is empty) and r=0 both hold. Step 1 is correct: the symmetric-algebra map is surjective as a map of sheaves, and clause (3) is proved from that input. I added lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded to Step 1 to justify that the map preserves degree. Gap (E1/C4): the last sentence of Step 2 identified the relative-Proj P^r_S of def-nagata-relative-projective-space with the P^N_Y of def-kun-projective without proof. def-kun-projective uses def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, S x_Z Proj Z[T], and def-nagata-relative-projective-space says it is not that definition. This is the step P(O^n)=P^{n-1}_S in the source. I repaired it with a new Step 3: lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists and the polynomial leaf give Proj_Z(Sym Z^{r+1}) = Proj Z[T]; def-nagata-graded-algebra-pullback-data identifies Sym O_S^{r+1} with g^*A_Z; lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary (closed) gives P^r_S = P({0..r};S). The repair creates no cycle. prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality and lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra are off-unit, non-closed statements that were used without being declared. I accepted both as generic tools and declared them in split_report.tool_uses. I also corrected a split_report summary that named a lemma no step cites.
